360	The walls would shake; a person's heart would
361	melt hearing it. Our dear in-law, the Gaon
362	Rabbi Eliyahu Abba Shaul, may he live long, related
363	that his father, great of the world, holy of holies, the Gaon and tzaddik, Rabbi Ben-Zion Abba Shaul,
364	would recite the bedtime Shema with such kavanah
365	that everyone standing next to him would tremble
366	from his acceptance of the yoke of Heaven.
367	Mrs. Reisha Slovitzky tells that she remembers the chassid Rabbi Nissan
368	Nemenov, who once was a guest in her parents' home, and she
369	saw her father looking at Rabbi Nissan, who had seen that he
370	had not yet gone to sleep all night; he only stood by the window and said the bedtime Shema in tears.
371	People come and rush through the Shema as if nothing happened, not a Shema
372	with all the enthusiasm, with all the fire — like the Alter Rebbe
373	of Chortzko.
374	Now, regarding what is told, one of his chassidim related,
375	that when he would begin to say the Shema, he would begin about an hour after midnight,
376	and he would finish at sunrise.
377	He would stop in the middle of the Shema.
378	About the Rebbe of Beit Yisrael, of Mamtzas Dof.
379	It is told that in his last months, before he passed away, he would say Tehillim often at night, before
380	he went up to his bed.
381	And afterward he would go and kiss all the mezuzot, in all the houses.
382	Then he would approach the Holy Ark and kiss the curtain.
383	Then he would recite the bedtime Shema; all this he did with great awe.
384	Great fear fell on everyone who saw him.
385	Understand, my teachers and masters, that saying the bedtime Shema means a person must know
386	how careful he must be.
387	It is not simple.
388	It is not simple at all, not simple at all.
389	They tell of the great Gaon Rabbi Isser Zalman, Rabbi Yisrael Isser Shapira, who
390	was told about the Gaon Rabbi Shapira, that when he recited the bedtime Shema, he would say it
391	with awe, trembling and sweat.
392	For example, the second verse of the first parashah: "And you shall love HaShem your God with all your heart, with all
393	your soul, and with all your might."
394	He would say it for ten minutes or a quarter of an hour.
395	What does a person say, "with all your heart"?
396	What is "with all your heart"?
397	"With all your soul" — to give over your soul; "with all your might" — all your money.
398	A person must think about what he is saying.
399	The students would stand behind him to see how he says it in holiness, to see how
400	he goes up on his bed to sleep.
401	It is an enormous and great responsibility when a person goes to sleep and watches over himself.
402	They tell of the holy Rabbi, author of the Bat Ayin of Biridsh; it is known that he was supremely holy.
403	You remember the famous story that in Tzfat there was an earthquake, all the houses fell; he
404	in his study hall told all the students to stand to the side where he was standing, and whoever stood next to him, nothing would happen
405	to him.
406	Indeed half the study hall fell, but the roof above him remained standing firm.
407	He would place his hands on the table while he was saying it.
408	He would take hold of the table and rise two handbreadths above the ground.
409	He would simply place his hands on the table and rise, to stand in the air, to disconnect from the matters of this
410	world, from the physical, from the material, and he would connect to the Creator of the world.
411	This is simply accepting the yoke of Heaven in order to reach the Shema.
412	He gives over his soul to the Holy One, blessed be He, in purity and holiness.
413	A person who says the Shema goes to sleep; sleep is one-sixtieth of death; a person gives over his soul.
414	And he is judged in Heaven; this is the fear of the Awesome Day. How is a person judged? Now I will also bring you the matter that a person
415	must also say vidui.
416	We say vidui; what is this vidui?
417	What is the way of the tzaddikim, what must they do?
418	How much a person must understand, with awesome trembling.
419	They were tzaddikim, simple people.
420	I saw several books about the simplest people who would weep, weep, weep, weep.
421	They wept truly while they recited the Shema.
422	It is told in the book Tefillat Yaakov: I saw that the reading of the Shema took the main place
423	each night; they sit and do cheshbon hanefesh
424	and weep. I will read you the holy Zohar; I found for you the Zohar
425	HaKadosh, how the holy Zohar says why one must prepare before a person goes to sleep.
426	He goes to deposit his soul with the Creator of the world, and there in Heaven the person's soul arrives, and they examine him, what
427	is happening with him, if he is a tzaddik, or, Heaven forbid, not in order.
428	Every single day, when night comes, a person must look, says the Zohar, to examine
429	and to check, all that was lost, all that day.
430	So that he may repent, and he should look constantly, so that he may repent fully.
431	As it is said, "And my sin is ever before me," so that he may repent.
432	The holy Zohar, Parashat Vayeshev, page 191, side a, says that every
433	day, when night comes, a person must look and examine everything he did that day, so that he may return
434	in teshuvah, and look always at all that he did, in order to return in complete teshuvah before his Creator, which
435	a person must do, must do every single day: cheshbon hanefesh. My father
436	had a large diary, and in this
437	diary there are hours; a big diary where every hour has a line, every hour,
438	one hour, two lines, and he writes every day, every hour, what he did now, what he did now, what he
439	did now, what he did now, what he did now, what he did now; at night he looks to see
440	all his deeds.
441	Tzaddikim would be satisfied and weep; they wasted no minutes of their time.
442	This is holiness.
443	A person must repent before the end, giving over his soul to the Creator of the world; one must understand.
444	Rabbi Maslovani related in the name of the holy Rabbi, Rabbi David Lubner, that once they saw Rabbi David Chaiki,
445	while reciting the Shema, say the verse "Into Your hand I entrust my spirit; You have redeemed me, HaShem, God of truth,"
446	and he fainted. They asked him, "Why did you faint?
447	What happened?"
448	Let me just tell you a story, a parable: To what is this similar? To a king who commanded all the people of his province
449	that each one bring before him all his possessions. Among them was one miserly man who brought a few
450	poor items, one small bundle. The moment he sees that all the ministers are bringing
451	abundant treasures, what does he bring?
452	Shame and fear seized him.
453	He says: when I come before the Holy One, blessed be He, "Into Your hand I entrust my spirit," among the angels and seraphim
454	who serve the Creator of the world, with what face do they come to deposit before Him?
455	Shame and humiliation, fear and trembling seized him.
456	This was the reason for his fainting.
457	They knew how to look and understand, to look with their spiritual eyes, what they are now about to do.
458	When a person goes to say the Shema he must think: what is he now about to do?
459	Is he going to say the Shema casually, or is he truly going to say the Shema,
460	to give over his soul, and also be judged in Heaven?
461	And there they examine him.
462	A person must understand this.
463	A person must understand this.
464	Everyone must understand what he is about to do, what he is about to feel.
465	"And every night, before he lies down and before he sleeps, a man should make a reckoning and vidui."
466	"...all that day, and he should repent of it, and compassion for the dead will come upon him," so that he be
467	in the likeness of death, which is seen in the world, and all the people of the world taste the taste of death, and at that hour
468	one must make a cheshbon and vidui, and confess, because that hour resembles death, and so the reckoning is required
469	and the cheshbon.
470	Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai says in the holy Zohar that every night, before a person lies down to sleep, before sleep,
471	he must do cheshbon hanefesh on the deeds he did that day.
472	He must repent for the bad deeds he did.
473	He asks the Holy One, blessed be He, to accept his teshuvah with mercy.
474	And why must he repent specifically at that hour?
475	The holy Zohar says that at that hour the Tree of Death dwells in the world.
476	All the people of the world taste the taste of death.
477	At that hour one must make a reckoning of the deeds.
478	And confess over them, because that hour is the hour of death.
479	A person must confess before he sleeps.
